findings.title: The Redis value type change is not compatible with existing live buffers
findings.body: Existing `span-buf:s:*` keys are Redis SETs written by the previous version, while this version issues `ZADD` against the same keys. Redis returns WRONGTYPE for that operation (and the new Lua script's `ZCARD`/`ZUNIONSTORE` calls also fail on those keys). During a rolling deployment, any active segment from the preceding version will make span processing fail rather than commit its Kafka batch, and old workers will likewise fail if they encounter a newly-created sorted set. Use versioned keys or an explicit migration/rollout strategy before changing the Redis datatype.

findings.title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate audit-log DateTime fields
findings.body: `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint` selects `OptimizedCursorPaginator` while ordering by `-datetime`, but this paginator's `get_item_key` passes the model's `datetime` value to `math.floor`/`math.ceil`. Unlike `DateTimePaginator`, it does not convert datetimes to a numeric cursor value. As soon as an authorized request uses `optimized_pagination=true` and the query returns an audit log entry, cursor construction raises `TypeError`, producing a 500 response instead of a paginated result.

findings.title: Advanced negative offsets are rejected by Django QuerySets
findings.body: The new advanced branch passes a negative `start_offset` directly to `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django QuerySet slicing explicitly rejects negative slice bounds with `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported`; it does not provide the claimed reverse-pagination behavior. Since `Cursor.from_string` accepts negative offsets, an advanced-pagination caller can trigger this error with a negative cursor rather than receiving a valid page.

findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE changes span timestamps when buffers overlap
findings.body: `ZUNIONSTORE` uses `SUM` as its default score aggregation. If a payload already exists in both the destination buffer and a buffer being merged—for example, when an at-least-once replay overlaps a previously buffered descendant—the resulting score becomes twice its `end_timestamp_precise` value. The score is now used to choose entries for `ZPOPMIN`, so these duplicated members look artificially newer and cause the wrong spans to be retained or evicted. Merge with an aggregation that preserves the timestamp (such as `MAX`) rather than the default sum.

findings.title: Insertion eviction ignores the configured segment span limit
findings.body: `SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans` remains a constructor setting, but the prior enforcement of that setting was removed from `_load_segment_data` and no limit is passed into this Lua script. The script instead always retains exactly 1000 members. Deployments configured with any other limit now silently discard spans at 1000 (and the default behavior changes from allowing 1001 members to retaining 1000), so the buffer configuration no longer controls its documented capacity.

findings.title: Reducing redirect traversal fragments deep out-of-order traces
findings.body: The redirect traversal bound was reduced from 10,000 to 1,000 without handling the case where the bound is reached. A valid deeply nested trace ingested from child toward root can create a redirect chain longer than 1,000 entries; subsequent spans then stop at an intermediate buffer and are mapped there instead of to the true segment root. This splits one trace into separately flushed segments and assigns incorrect segment IDs.
